# CI Pipeline

GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs in two tiers, gated by `ci-gate`, the single required check that fans in every other job:

- **Tier A, every pull_request push:** `fmt`, `clippy` (which also runs `just doc`), `rust-version` (fails if a package's `rust-version` differs from the channel in `rust-toolchain.toml`; `just check-rust-version`), `typos`, `shellcheck`, `image-ca-certificates` (builds the Dockerfile's `base` stage and fails if the image would trust a CA in `.github/scripts/distrusted-roots.txt`), `lock-downgrade` (see below), `third-party-license`, `test` (postgres:16, the oldest version the project tests), the memory leg of `compat-librdkafka` and `compat-franz-go`, and `compat-kafka-java`, which runs the tests in `compat/kafka-java/tests.allow` (Apache Kafka 3.9.1's own integration tests) against the memory engine. `compat-kafka-java` is experimental: it has `continue-on-error`, so a failure does not fail `ci-gate`.
- **Tier B, once per merge-queue entry (`merge_group`); a push to `main` runs only the cache-saving subset:** the `build-storage` matrix (one build per storage engine, `turso` included) and `build-storage-lake` (one build per lake format on `dynostore`), `test` on postgres:16 only, the postgres and sqlite compat legs (S3 compat runs in the nightly Tier C, which also runs `test` on Postgres 17, 18 and 19beta4), the `compat-librdkafka` legs at the oldest librdkafka version CI tests (v2.3.0) on every engine, experimental until they have a record in CI, `cargo-publish-dry-run`, `src`, `release` (the static Linux binaries), `macos` (`aarch64-apple-darwin`) and `windows` (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`), each a compile-only `cargo check` that does the full release build only on a `v*` tag, packed as a tarball for macOS and a zip for Windows (the scheduled Tier C workflow (twice a day) builds both releases on main), `smoke` (the `nisshi-smoke-test` suite: Kafka CLI tools from Kafka 3.9 and 4.3 against an image built in the job from `release`'s binaries on postgres, sqlite, memory and s3, on x86 and arm), `smoke-oldest-client` (the same suite with the Kafka 3.7 CLI tools, the oldest client CI tests, on postgres, sqlite, memory and s3 on x86 only); `smoke-report` puts every leg of both in one pass/fail grid in the step summary. The push to `main` repeats a tree that the queue already tested, so it runs only `fmt`, `clippy`, `test`, `cargo-publish-dry-run`, `release`, `macos`, `windows` and `third-party-license` (the jobs that save a cache), plus `changes`, `rust-version`, `typos`, `shellcheck`, `image-ca-certificates`, `lock-downgrade` (whose steps skip there) and `ci-gate`. Every other job carries `github.ref != 'refs/heads/main'`, and `ci-gate` names the jobs that may skip there, so a new job must run on main until someone adds it to that list.
- **Publishing, from the scheduled Tier C run on main and on `v*` tags only:** `ci.yml` pushes no image. The scheduled Tier C workflow (`tier-c.yml`) pushes the multi-arch `edge` image of main's tip, also tagged `main` for external consumers until a follow-up drops that tag. Its `edge-gate` job requires a successful merge-queue run and a successful push run of `ci.yml` for the tip, and `edge-publish` builds the image from the `image-*` binaries of that push run, so nothing compiles. If a merge lands during the nightly run, or its push run is still in progress, the gate skips the publish and `edge` trails the tip until the next run. A `v*` tag doesn't trigger `ci.yml`: it runs `release.yml`, which calls `ci.yml` through `workflow_call` (so the full Tier B run happens on the tagged commit), an `on-main` check that the tagged commit is on main, a `release-tag` check (`.github/scripts/check-release-tag.sh`, tested in `workflow-lint.yml`) that the tag's version is the tagged commit's `Cargo.toml` version and that a stable tag has a `CHANGELOG.md` section, and `release-readiness` (`release-readiness-check.yaml`), which starts once `on-main` and `release-tag` pass, re-runs `guardian-scan.yaml` in trunk mode on the tag and blocks on the Guardian gate's verdict. Only when all four pass does it publish, one job after another: `publish-image` (semver and `latest`), `github-release` (holds `contents: write`, runs in the `release` environment, uploads the tarballs and the Windows zip, and sets no body), then `publish-crates`. The `/cut-release` skill (`.claude/skills/cut-release/`) opens the release PR, tags its squash commit, and after the run sets the release body with `gh release edit`. If only `release-readiness` fails, an `override` job waits in the `release-override` environment, whose required reviewers are repo admins: approving it publishes over the failed check, a Guardian block and a scanner outage alike, and rejecting it ends the run with nothing published. The environment prevents self-review and admin bypass, and the `override` job refuses to run if either is off or if the run records no approval of `release-override` from someone other than whoever pushed the tag or started the re-run, so a second admin has to approve: whoever pushed the tag or started a re-run can't. The on-main check does not stop a tag whose commit edits the workflow, so a tag ruleset is the control for who may create `v*` tags. No other run pushes anything, and a failed leg can't leave a partial release. `release` needs only `typos` (and `changes`), and `smoke` needs only `release`, so `test`, `macos`, `windows` and the build matrices run beside the `release` -> `smoke` chain instead of ahead of it. `test` doesn't wait for `fmt` or `clippy`.
- **Cache:** `test` saves the Rust cache under the `dev` shared key on main; the compat jobs restore it and never save. `build-storage` and `build-storage-lake` use no cache, because `cargo check` reuses little of a full build. rust-cache hashes every `CARGO*`, `CC*`, `CFLAGS*`, `CXX*`, `CMAKE*` and `RUST*` variable into the key, so set `RUST_BACKTRACE` and `RUST_LOG` on the step that needs them, not on the job.
- **Reports:** the `test` jobs (in `ci.yml` and `tier-c.yml`) run nextest and the doctests as separate steps, because doctests write no JUnit report; the doctests also run after a nextest failure. Both jobs then run the `.github/actions/test-reports` composite action, so a PR's `ci.yml` run exercises the steps the nightly run uses. Its `junit-summary.py` turns the JUnit report into the job's step summary: results per suite, the 10 slowest tests, and up to 30 failures, each with its message or the end of its stderr. The action uploads a `test-reports-<postgres image>` artifact with `junit.xml` and `cargo-timing.html`. `ci-gate` adds a table of job and step durations to its summary and uploads it as the `timings` artifact; it needs `actions: read`, so `release.yml`'s `ci` job grants it too. Every report step continues on error, so a report never changes a job's result.

Merging goes through a merge queue: "Merge when ready" queues the PR, the queue re-runs CI on it against the current tip of `main`, and squash-merges it if everything is green: the PR title becomes the commit's subject and the PR description its body. Tier B is skipped on same-repo PRs only while the `MERGE_QUEUE` repository variable is `on`; with it unset, they run everything. Fork PRs can't read the variable, so Tier B is always skipped on them and runs in the queue. The other required checks come from `codeql.yml`, `workflow-lint.yml`, `dependencies.yml` and `pr-title.yml` (the PR title must follow Conventional Commits; see `CONTRIBUTING.md`).

On a pull_request, a `changes` job in `ci.yml`, `codeql.yml`, `dependencies.yml` and `fuzz.yml` skips the Rust jobs when every changed path is CI config those workflows don't read, or prose. The skip list is `.github/scripts/ci-changes.sh`, tested by `ci-changes.test.sh`; the `changes` jobs run the base branch's copy, so a PR can't widen its own skip list.

The `lock-downgrade` job runs `.github/scripts/check-lock-downgrade.py`, which fails a PR whose `Cargo.lock` or `fuzz/Cargo.lock` moves a package or a dependency edge to a lower version than the base branch. `cargo update -p` and Dependabot can re-point crates that they were not asked to update at older copies already in the lockfile (rust-lang/cargo#14446). After `cargo update -p`, run `git show origin/main:Cargo.lock > /tmp/base.lock && python3 .github/scripts/check-lock-downgrade.py /tmp/base.lock Cargo.lock`. For each line it prints, point that package's `dependencies` entry back at main's version, then run `cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 >/dev/null` to confirm that cargo accepts the lockfile. A deliberate downgrade merges through an admin bypass. The job checks only the pull_request run: a merge-queue entry passes it unchecked, so a lockfile that changes when the queue puts the PR on a newer `main` is not checked again.

`guardian-scan.yaml` reports supply-chain findings to Guardian, and its `Guardian scan gate` job is the one check a ruleset requires from it. On a PR it runs FOSSA's licensing and vulnerability checks in report-only mode and uploads nothing. Fork PRs, Dependabot PRs and merge-queue entries skip the scans and pass the gate with a logged reason. On push to main it also builds the musl image (with `cargo auditable`, like `release`), scans it with Prisma, syncs both results to Guardian and blocks on Guardian's vulnerability gate and on FOSSA's licensing check (a license the FOSSA policy denies, or a dependency with no license), and then `Update release manifest` writes the manifest row if the commit is still main's tip. `.github/scripts/guardian-scan-context.sh` decides the mode (pr, queue, trunk, branch) and `guardian-scan-gate.sh` decides the gate's verdict. Each has a self-test, and both run at the start of every scan. The scripts run from the workflow's own commit, never from the ref being scanned, and a dispatched tag must be spelled `refs/tags/<tag>` to count as a release (a bare `v1.2.3` is treated as a branch). Its secrets are split across two environments. `guardian` holds only `FOSSA_API_KEY`, for PR runs. `guardian-trunk` holds that plus `GUARDIAN_URL`, `GUARDIAN_API_TOKEN` and the three `PRISMACLOUD_*` credentials, and its deployment policy admits only the main branch and `v*` tags. The repository also needs read access to the `maas-build-actions` package, the `solace-cloud-manifest-rw` custom property set to `true`, and the OIDC sub customization `[repo_property_solace-cloud-manifest-rw, repository_owner, ref]`, which the manifest role's trust policy matches for the main branch only.

`fuzz.yml` runs the cargo-fuzz targets in `fuzz/`: briefly on every PR (report-only, not a required check) and for longer nightly. Which targets run in each, and for how long, is set in `fuzz/ci-targets.json`; see `fuzz/README.md`. Run the PR set locally with `just fuzz-ci pr`.
